issues: The new restart step uses no randomness: each centre moves 0.02 away from its nearest neighbour, so every restart from the same start begins at the same point and the restarts lose their diversity. This probably explains why the candidate (2.9254) falls back to about the level of the original starting script. It is a design flaw, not a measurement bug.
Only 1 run per side; |z|~1.5 is not significant, but it points toward worse, so reject is reasonable.
Recomputed z = (−2.9327 − (−2.9254)) / (0.0034·√2) ≈ −1.52, which roughly matches the harness's −1.496. The small gap is most likely rounding in the shown values.
No file or network access, no pasted coordinates, no change to the validity check or repair step; the +1e-12 guard prevents division by zero when two centres coincide.
